key_differences_summary: APY is for retirement saving by workers aged 18–40; NSPG is for student financial aid (under 30, pursuing first PG)
APY pays Rs. 1,000–5,000/month from age 60 onwards; NSPG pays Rs. 15,000/month during first-year PG studies
APY has no application deadline; NSPG has yearly opening/closing dates set by NSP
APY excludes income-tax payers; NSPG excludes those who have completed a previous PG degree
recommendation: These are completely different schemes for different life stages: Choose APY if you are an unorganised-sector worker (non-tax-payer, aged 18–40) wanting guaranteed old-age income security. Choose NSPG if you are a meritorious student under 30 pursuing your first postgraduate degree and need financial support. They can potentially both apply to you if you meet both criteria — they are not mutually exclusive. For final eligibility confirmation and application, visit the official portals or contact the respective ministries.
